summary:
AgroShift AI is an intelligent agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers adapt to climate change, water scarcity, and declining soil health. Developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026’s “Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data,” our project transforms complex scientific data into practical, sustainable agricultural strategies.

Farmers can select their land on an interactive map and explore personalized production plans for the coming years. Our platform integrates NASA Earth observation and climate data with soil characteristics, crop requirements, water availability, and economic factors. Using agricultural science, mathematical models, and multi-criteria optimization, AgroShift AI compares alternative crop rotation strategies based on expected yields, irrigation requirements, production costs, profitability, and climate-related risks.

Rather than prescribing a single solution, AgroShift AI presents multiple scenarios, allowing farmers to choose strategies aligned with their resources and priorities. The platform also explains the scientific reasoning behind its recommendations and highlights uncertainties in future conditions.

Our goal is to make advanced agricultural intelligence accessible, helping farmers make informed decisions, use resources more efficiently, and build resilient farming systems for the future.
details:
AgroShift AI — Project Details

Overview

AgroShift AI is a data-driven agricultural decision-support platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data" challenge. It aims to help farmers develop more sustainable, profitable, and climate-resilient agricultural strategies by combining Earth observation data, soil characteristics, crop requirements, and mathematical decision models.

How It Works

The process begins when a farmer selects an agricultural field through our interactive map and provides relevant information, including irrigation capacity, cultivation history, and production priorities.

AgroShift AI brings together multiple scientific data sources:

  • NASA POWER: Historical temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation.
  • NASA GPM and SMAP: Additional precipitation and soil moisture information where available.
  • ISRIC SoilGrids: Soil properties such as pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, and soil texture.
  • FAO agricultural resources: Crop requirements, water management methodologies, and crop development parameters.
  • Regional agricultural data: Crop yields, production costs, and market information where accessible.

The platform processes these inputs using agricultural science and mathematical decision-making methods.

Water requirements can be evaluated through FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration calculations and crop-specific coefficients. Crop suitability is assessed by comparing environmental conditions with biological requirements.

Multi-criteria decision analysis and optimization methods are used to compare alternative crop rotation strategies across future growing seasons.

Each scenario is evaluated according to relevant indicators, including estimated productivity, water requirements, economic outcomes, soil sustainability, and climate-related risks.

Rather than prescribing a single agricultural decision, AgroShift AI presents multiple alternatives, enabling farmers to select strategies that best match their resources and priorities.

Innovation and Benefits

Our approach focuses on the long-term consequences of agricultural decisions rather than isolated, single-season recommendations.

AgroShift AI aims to provide:

  • Multi-year crop rotation planning.
  • Personalized crop suitability assessments.
  • Scientific water requirement calculations.
  • Comparative economic and productivity analyses.
  • Climate and drought scenario evaluation.
  • Transparent explanations of data sources and modeling assumptions.

The platform distinguishes observed data, modeled estimates, and simulated scenarios to communicate uncertainty responsibly.

Technologies and Development

AgroShift AI is developed as a web-based agricultural intelligence platform, combining interactive geographic visualization, external scientific data sources, data processing, and computational modeling.

Our development process incorporates AI-assisted programming tools to accelerate implementation, debugging, interface design, and technical research. Scientific modeling and agricultural decision logic are treated as distinct components that require validation against established methodologies and real-world observations.

Intended Impact

Our long-term objective is to make advanced agricultural planning accessible to farmers and agricultural professionals.

By transforming complex environmental data into understandable production strategies, AgroShift AI aims to support efficient water use, improved resource allocation, reduced exposure to climate-related risks, and more informed agricultural decisions.

Our mission is not to predict the future with certainty, but to help farmers make better decisions in the face of uncertainty.
